high.title: Ringgit ends lower on Fed rate hike expectations
high.summary: The ringgit depreciated to 4.0920/4.0965 against the USD, driven by Fed rate hike expectations reinforced by stronger-than-expected US JOLTS job openings data. Asian currencies broadly weakened as investors anticipate further US monetary tightening. This directly impacts Malaysian import costs, inflation, and business financing conditions.

high.title: Bursa reverses earlier gains to end lower
high.summary: The FBM KLCI fell 7.23 points to close at 1,656.83, reversing intraday gains due to late profit-taking amid cautious sentiment and a lack of fresh market catalysts. Persistent foreign selling pressure continues, though local institutional net buying of RM199 million provides some support. Near-term sentiment remains fragile pending global interest rate clarity.

high.title: Bursa pares earlier losses to end slightly lower
high.summary: The FBM KLCI closed slightly lower but recovered from earlier losses due to afternoon bargain hunting, with mid- and small-cap stocks showing resilience. Market sentiment was shaped by AI valuation concerns, the fragile US-Iran ceasefire, and China's export controls on Japanese companies. The KLCI is nearing oversold territory, potentially signalling a buying opportunity for selective investors.

high.title: Stocks adrift, oil up as US-Iran halt renewed attacks
high.summary: Global markets traded cautiously amid renewed US-Iran ceasefire hopes following tit-for-tat strikes near the Strait of Hormuz, a critical oil shipping lane. Brent crude climbed 0.85% to US$72.6 a barrel and WTI rose over 1%, impacting energy-sensitive Malaysian markets and the ringgit. Asian indices were broadly weaker, with mixed US futures reflecting ongoing geopolitical uncertainty.

high.title: Bursa retreats at open as sentiment turns cautious
high.summary: Bursa Malaysia opened lower with the FBM KLCI falling 5.70 points to 1,662.04 as Wall Street's tech-led decline and escalating US-Iran geopolitical tensions weighed on sentiment. Analysts noted the cautious market undertone and recommended selective accumulation at current levels. The index was expected to trade within the 1,665–1,675 range for the session.

high.title: Ringgit extends gains against US dollar, regional peers
high.summary: The ringgit is extending gains against the US dollar as US economic data showed underlying weakness, with Q1 2026 GDP at 2.1% but consumer spending rising only 0.5%. Trimmed expectations for aggressive Fed rate hikes have pulled US yields lower, relieving pressure on Asian currencies including the ringgit. US PCE inflation came in at 4.1% in May, in line with expectations, further shaping Fed policy outlook relevant to Malaysian currency and capital markets.

medium.title: US factory activity grows at slower pace in June
medium.summary: The ISM manufacturing index dipped to 53.3% in June, remaining above the growth threshold but reflecting growing business pessimism tied to the Iran conflict and tariffs. Price volatility was flagged as a key concern by respondents. This signals potential headwinds for global trade and export-reliant Malaysian manufacturers.

medium.title: Bursa edges higher on US-Iran peace hopes, Wall Street gains
medium.summary: The FBM KLCI opened marginally higher at 1,664.65, supported by Wall Street's tech-led rally and optimism over US-Iran peace prospects. Market breadth was positive early in the session with gainers outpacing decliners. However, overall sentiment remained subdued, limiting upside momentum.

medium.title: Ringgit opens firmer on weaker US consumer confidence data
medium.summary: The ringgit rose to 4.0775/4.0870 against the USD after US consumer confidence came in below expectations at 91.2 points, tempering Fed rate hike bets. Caution persisted ahead of the US nonfarm payrolls report, with consensus estimates at 114,000 for June. The currency's trajectory remains closely tied to US monetary policy signals rather than oil price movements.

medium.title: Ringgit closes lower ahead of key US economic data
medium.summary: The ringgit depreciated to 4.0825/4.0870 against the US dollar by close of day, retreating from an earlier intraday high of RM4.04. The US Dollar Index rose 0.23% to 101.338, weighing on the local currency. Key US data releases including JOLTS and Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index are expected to influence the ringgit's near-term direction.

medium.title: Bursa ends on a softer note
medium.summary: The FBM KLCI eased 1.85 points to close at 1,664.06, as persistent foreign selling and external uncertainties subdued domestic sentiment despite broadly higher regional equities. Analysts note that the recent pullback has made selected blue-chip valuations more attractive, potentially drawing bargain hunters. Domestic institutional buying is expected to cushion further downside.

medium.title: Bursa gains in early trade on improved risk sentiment
medium.summary: The FBM KLCI edged up marginally at the open to 1,666.15, with positive market breadth as gainers outnumbered losers. However, analysts anticipated a lacklustre session with the index expected to trade within the 1,660-1,670 range amid ongoing Middle East tensions and external uncertainties. Low trading volume signals continued investor caution.

medium.title: Ringgit gains in early trade on weaker US Dollar Index
medium.summary: The ringgit opened stronger at 4.0605/4.0730 against the greenback, supported by a 0.25% decline in the DXY to 101.10. Analysts expected the currency to trade within a 4.06 to 4.08 range as markets awaited key US data releases including JOLTS and Conference Board Consumer Confidence figures. Improved consumer confidence in June was anticipated.

medium.title: Ringgit strengthens against major regional currencies
medium.summary: The ringgit appreciated to 4.0680/4.0735 against the US dollar at close, recovering from Friday's 4.0860/4.0910 level, supported by lower crude oil prices amid US-Iran peace negotiations. WTI and Brent crude hovered at US$70.22 and US$72.69 per barrel respectively. A series of key US economic data releases this week, including nonfarm payrolls and ISM indices, are expected to drive further currency movement.

medium.title: Ringgit slightly higher against greenback, supported by low oil prices
medium.summary: The ringgit opened slightly stronger at 4.0855 against the US dollar, supported by continued shipping activity through the Strait of Hormuz and expectations of ongoing US-Iran negotiations. Analysts project the USD/MYR pair to hover between RM4.08 and RM4.10, with oil prices remaining a key driver. Stability in the ringgit is significant for Malaysian importers, exporters, and foreign investment flows.

medium.title: Six-month extension for stamp duty disclosure programme
medium.summary: LHDN extended its voluntary stamp duty disclosure programme, giving businesses and individuals more time to comply with the new stamp duty self-assessment system without facing penalties. Instruments executed between January 1, 2023 and December 31, 2025 are eligible for penalty exemption if stamped and paid before December 31 this year. This is relevant to Malaysian property transactions and business agreements executed during that period.
